zigosity.notes: No twin study design or zygosity information reported.

age_min.notes: Minimum age from Ethiopian cohort infants. Study reports multiple cohorts with varying age ranges.

age_max.notes: Maximum age from Tanzanian adult cohort. Study encompasses multiple age groups across three newly sequenced cohorts.

age_years.notes: Study reports age ranges and means for multiple cohorts but not a single age value for all participants.

antibiotics_current_use.notes: No information on antibiotic use reported in the paper.

bmi.notes: Paper mentions BMI as a factor considered but states 'no significant differences with all four clades being identified across all age groups and BMI categories' without reporting actual BMI values.

dietary_restriction.notes: No individual dietary restrictions reported for participants; diet discussed at population level (Westernized vs non-Westernized).

disease.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
disease.notes: Study focused on newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts from Ghana, Tanzania, and Ethiopia. Paper also analyzes public metagenomes from disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, etc.) but those were not newly sampled in this study.

disease_details.notes: Newly sampled participants were healthy. Disease analysis in the paper involved public datasets, not detailed disease information for primary cohort.

disease_response_orr.notes: No treatment response data reported; study is a metagenomic and genomic analysis of P. copri complex.

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: Not applicable to this microbiome study.

disease_response_recist.notes: Not applicable; no RECIST criteria used in microbiome analysis.

feces_phenotype.notes: Study analyzed stool samples but no specific fecal phenotype measurements reported.

fmt_id.notes: No fecal microbiota transplantation study; this is a population genomics and metagenomic analysis study.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Study included infants and mothers in Ethiopian cohort but no birth weight data reported.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: No infant feeding method data reported despite inclusion of infant samples.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: No gestational age at birth reported.

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: No information on preterm vs term birth reported.

obgyn_birth_control.notes: No information on oral contraceptive use reported.

obgyn_lactating.notes: Study included mother-infant pairs but no lactation status reported.

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: Study included mothers in Ethiopian cohort but no current pregnancy status specified.

value: Four distinct clades of P. copri (A, B, C, D) proposed to constitute the P. copri complex
P. copri genomes reconstructed: 1,023 total (17 isolates, 1,006 metagenome-assembled genomes)
Metagenomes analyzed: 6,874 publicly available from 36 datasets across 6 continents and 25 countries
Additional 272 metagenomes sequenced from Ethiopia (50), Ghana (44), and Tanzania (68)
Ancient metagenomes analyzed: Iceman (5,300-year-old) and Mexican coprolites (1,300±100 BP)
Clade diversification estimated 6.5 million years ago (clade B split)
Clades A, D, C diversification: 3.5-2.5 million years ago
Within-clade differentiation relatively recent, post-emergence of Homo sapiens (~315 ka)
High prevalence of all four clades consistent with non-Westernized populations across Africa, Oceania, South America, Asia
No strong evidence that specific clades associated with colorectal cancer, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, or IBD
Functional diversity includes distinct carbohydrate metabolism repertoires between clades
Multi-generational dietary modifications proposed as driver of reduced P. copri prevalence in Westernized populations
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: P. copri encompasses four distinct clades...we propose the term Prevotella copri complex...P. copri began to diversify (split of clade B) ~6.5 million years ago
uncurated_metadata.notes: Key findings and contextual information about P. copri complex characterization, evolutionary history, and biogeographical distribution.

host_species.evidence_quote: Prevotella copri is a common human gut microbe. All subjects enrolled in this study included infants and adults from Ghana, Tanzania and Ethiopia
host_species.section: Abstract, Experimental Model and Subject Details
host_species.notes: Inferred from context: study focuses on human gut microbiome and explicitly describes human subjects sampled.

The schema fields are primarily designed for clinical and individual-level patient metadata, which are largely absent from this study. Newly sequenced cohorts (Ghana, Tanzania, Ethiopia; n=162 individuals) were healthy and provided minimal clinical metadata. Most demographic information is summarized at the cohort level rather than per-individual.

The paper focuses on P. copri genetic diversity, population structure, and ancient metagenomes rather than individual participant clinical outcomes or phenotypes.

Biomarker values represent microbial prevalence percentages and genetic distances, not traditional clinical biomarkers.
